newsitem.title: USA: Stanhome says to sell Hamilton unit.
newsitem.headline: Stanhome says to sell Hamilton unit.

text.p: Stanhome Inc said Wednesday it will sell its Hamilton Direct Response Group for about $46 million, and will focus on its branded giftware business.
The company said the deal will result in a first quarter earnings per share charge of $1.95.
The company said it has signed an agreement to sell Hamilton to The Bradford Group, a privately held marketer of giftwares. The deal includes repayment of intercompany debt.
The company said it will take a one-time, primarily non-cash, after-tax charge of $35 million in connection with the sale.
The charge consists mainly of the write-down of goodwill and associated transaction and severance costs.
The company said the Hamilton sale is one of several measures it is taking to build shareholder value.
The company said it will evaluate its options for its Worldwide Direct Selling Group business, with the assistance of Goldman, Sachs & Co.
A company spokesman said it is considering selling the business, spinning it off, or arranging a buyout.
The company also said it would apply the proceeds from the Hamilton deal and any transaction involving Direct Selling toward further share repurchases under the on-going share repurchase program.
The company said it will also close its corporate headquarters and eventually sell the building.
A company spokesman said 52 people work at the facility. Most of the position will be eliminated, and a few will be moved to other units.
The company also said it will begin a long-term license agreement between Bradford and its Enesco Giftware Group. The agreement would produce incremental, on-going royalties for Enesco.
The company declined to disclose a dollar value on the royalties.
